thread:
morgan: Quick heads-up — ran nsys on staging-gpu-3 with the new batching heuristics. Timeline shows 4 kernels taking ~85% of GPU time; not the usual matmul hotspot. Pasting the trimmed output and notes below.

jin: Can you drop the top kernels (nvprof/ncu output)? even just the top 5 is fine.

morgan: ```
Top kernels by GPU time:
1) kv_cache_lookup_kernel       calls=1200  total_ms=42.1  pct=46%
2) continuous_batch_pack_v3     calls=600   total_ms=18.3  pct=20%
3) softmax_dropout_fwd          calls=2400  total_ms=12.7  pct=14%
4) tensor_shard_sync            calls=90    total_ms=8.9   pct=10%
other kernels: small (10%)
```

alex: kv_cache_lookup_kernel at ~46% is a surprise. Is that the prefetch+merge path or the eviction scan? We only expected matmuls to dominate.

morgan: It's the prefetch+merge path — nvtx regions line up with host-side prefetch dispatch then a bunch of tiny kernels for lookup/merge. I also see long host gaps between kernel launches in the perfetto trace: https://perfetto/trace/abc123 (private).

sophia: Do we have SM util / occupancy metrics from the run? that will tell if it's compute or memory bound.

morgan: ```
NVPROF / NCU snippets:
- avg_sm_efficiency: 32%
- achieved_occupancy: 0.45
- gld_throughput: 1.8 GB/s (avg)
- shared_mem_efficiency: 28%
```

jin: Low SM efficiency + low shared_mem_efficiency + high kv kernel time => likely memory-bound and uncoalesced accesses in the KV path (warp divergence or scatter loads). Also check if the KV indexing uses 64-bit keys which cause extra divergence.

morgan: Agree. The timeline also shows these kv kernels are very frequent but short; launch overhead / CPU scheduling could be amplifying cost. I noticed we recently added a batching lock around prefetch dispatch (PR #4421) — might be introducing host-side serialization.

alex: Two hypotheses: (A) CPU-side batching lock is serializing launches -> idle gaps; (B) kernel implementation has poor memory access pattern -> low throughput. We should triage both.

morgan: Plan I ran: (1) microbench a single-threaded KV lookup kernel with coalesced vs scatter index to measure gld_throughput; (2) re-run nsys with nvprof metrics: gld_efficiency, l1_tex_hit_rate, dram_read_throughput; (3) flip out the batching lock in a local branch to measure host-side gap reduction.

jin: I'll run the microbench for different batch sizes (1, 8, 32, 64) and compare latency/throughput. Also add nvprof: --metrics gld_efficiency,sm_efficiency,achieved_occupancy.

sophia: I'll audit batching-heuristics counters to see how often prefetch dispatch is stalling due to lock contention and whether the new heuristic increases number of tiny dispatches.

morgan: Quick data point: when I disabled prefetch in the run, GPU time shifted back to matmul kernels and latency for end-to-end inference increased slightly but per-token GPU cost dropped (weird). So prefetch is doing useful work but at a worse GPU-efficiency cost.

alex: Sounds like we need a middle ground: larger aggregated prefetch batches with a coalesced lookup path.

morgan: Action items: morgan -> instrument KV index coalescing + push microbench; jin -> run microbench and capture nvprof metrics; sophia -> gather batching counters and produce a short table of dispatch sizes. We'll sync tomorrow morning.

perf-bot: Deploy notice — rolling canary of batching-heuristics v2 applied to staging-gpu-3 at 1823456810.

alex: ack, thanks. :thumbsup:
